Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexTel Communications Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexTel Communications' Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q2 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas.

First, our new product and service launches exceeded expectations, delivering substantial revenue uplift and subscriber gains. Second, we continue to see favorable trends in churn rates, with meaningful improvements driven by network enhancements and bundling. Third, subscriber acquisition costs have trended downward through efficiencies and smarter marketing. Fourth, our cost of revenue management is balancing growth investments with margin discipline. Fifth, ARPU expansion from pricing actions and bundles is accelerating. And sixth, our dividend remains rock-solid, supported by robust free cash flow for shareholder returns. We're strategically investing across these to build our converged 5G media ecosystem.

Mike Chen: Thank you, John. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $28.5 billion, an increase of 12% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $7.4 billion, resulting in a margin of 26%. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $7.2 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here on the West Coast. Diving deeper into one of our key growth drivers, I'd like to highlight the impact of our new product and service launches on revenue and subscriber growth. NexTel is at the forefront of converging telecommunications and media, leveraging our nationwide 5G spectrum holdings—much like our peers at Verizon and T-Mobile—and our proprietary streaming platform, NexStream, to capture share in a market where cord-cutting accelerated to 7.2 million U.S. pay-TV households last year, per Nielsen data.

In Q2, these launches delivered $1.4 billion in incremental revenue, representing a 38% year-over-year increase from these initiatives alone, and drove 1.2 million net subscriber additions across postpaid mobile, broadband, and media segments. This not only boosted our overall revenue by the 12% I mentioned but also lifted blended ARPU by 4.2% to $58.70, outpacing industry averages reported by the CTIA.

Breaking it down: Our 5G Ultra Home Pro fixed wireless access service, rolled out in 15 additional MSAs—including high-density markets like Atlanta, Phoenix, and Dallas—hit 450,000 new broadband subscribers, a 62% quarter-over-quarter ramp-up. This generated $420 million in Q2 revenue, with an annualized run-rate now exceeding $2.1 billion. Penetration in rural and suburban overlays reached 18%, fueled by our mmWave and C-band spectrum efficiency, delivering gigabit speeds at 40% below traditional fiber CAPEX. Regionally, the Southeast saw 35% of adds due to underserved Tier 2 markets, while California contributed 22% amid our edge partnerships with AWS for low-latency gaming. Churn here is sub-1%, versus the 2.1% industry FWA average, thanks to our AI-driven predictive maintenance, reducing outages by 45%.

Next, NexStream+, our ad-supported streaming bundle launched in April with zero-rated Disney+, Paramount+, and our exclusive NexOriginals content slate—including live sports rights akin to Peacock's NBA deal—added 520,000 media subscribers, pushing total video subs to 14.2 million. Revenue impact: $380 million in Q2, up 55% year-over-year, with 65% from ARPU uplift now at $14.50 per month via dynamic ad insertion tech from our FreeWheel platform. In Europe, where we expanded via our Vodafone JV, we captured 120,000 adds in the UK and Germany, offsetting regulatory headwinds like the EU's DMA by emphasizing AVOD models. This positions us against Netflix's password crackdown, which drove 2 million U.S. adds industry-wide in Q1 per Antenna data.

Third, enterprise 5G Private Networks and Edge Media Services, targeting media production and live events—think mirroring AT&T's WarnerMedia synergies—onboarded 150 enterprise clients, including regional broadcasters and Hollywood studios. This contributed $280 million in high-margin revenue at 72% EBITDA, with 85,000 indirect consumer subs via bundled employee perks. APAC expansion through our Singtel partnership added $90 million here, tapping ASEAN's 5G video boom projected at 25% CAGR by GSMA.

Finally, our AI-Powered 5G Mobile Unlimited Max plan, with network slicing for 4K streaming and XR experiences, saw postpaid phone net adds of 620,000, including 40% upgrades from 4G. Revenue: $320 million incremental, lifting mobile service revenue 15% year-over-year. Northeast U.S. markets led with 28% of adds, driven by our densified small-cell deployments amid spectrum auctions.

Strategically, these align with our 'Converged 5G Media Ecosystem' thesis: bundling telco reliability with content stickiness to combat 1.8% broadband churn industry-wide per FCC. We've embedded Open RAN pilots for 20% OpEx savings, enabling aggressive pricing—FWA at $60 per month versus Comcast's $80. Forward-looking, we expect these to add $5.8 billion in 2024 revenue run-rate, with subscriber growth accelerating to 5 million annualized as we hit 85% 5G coverage. Risks include supply chain pressures on CPE devices, but our diversified vendor strategy with Nokia and Ericsson mitigates this. Overall, these initiatives underscore NexTel's pivot to high-ARPU, low-churn services in a $500 billion TAM blending telecom and streaming.

Turning now to churn rate analysis—a critical leading indicator of customer loyalty and long-term revenue sustainability. At NexTel, we track it across postpaid wireless, prepaid wireless, fixed broadband, and NexStream on a blended basis. In Q2, our overall blended churn rate improved to 1.8%, down 25 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 2.05% and 40 basis points year-over-year from 2.2% last year. This marks our best quarterly performance in two years, ahead of the 2.1% industry average per New Street Research.

By segment: Postpaid wireless at 0.85% blended monthly—phone at 0.72%, down 10 bps QoQ; connected devices at 1.1%. Prepaid at 3.2%, improved from 3.5% YoY via Go5G Prepaid bundles. Fixed broadband at 1.15%, down 30 bps YoY from XGS-PON fiber overbuilds. NexusStream SVOD at 4.1% quarterly, better than 4.6% prior. Enterprise and wholesale under 0.5%.

Trends show a downward trajectory over six quarters: postpaid from 1.05% peak amid macro headwinds to sub-0.9% now, mirroring T-Mobile but with media differentiation. Broadband stabilized post seasonal moves, NexusStream down 110 bps with sports investments.

Key positive drivers: Network superiority from $12 billion CapEx in 5G SA and mmWave, with 85% mid-band coverage at 450 Mbps median speeds—20% faster than peers per Ookla—cutting buffering 35% and lifting retention 15%. Bundling like Nexus One at $110/month yields 0.6% churn vs. standalone. Content moat from NBA/NFL rights, with sports viewers 40% stickier; ad-tier at $7.99 has 25% lower churn.

Headwinds navigated: Economic pressures added 20 bps in prepaid amid Sun Belt unemployment; price hikes temporary 15 bps hit, recaptured 70%; MVNO poaching and streaming mergers 10-15 bps; copper decommissioning resolved.

Regionally: U.S. at 1.6%, Northeast 0.7%; rural Midwest 2.2% improving with FWA; Europe JV 2.4% amid price caps, stabilizing via Open RAN; LATAM 4.5% prepaid-heavy but fintech cutting 50 bps QoQ; APAC under 1%.

Proactive retention via AI churn prediction at 92% accuracy recovers 28%; edge computing and Nexus Rewards yield 3x ROI. Q3 guide 1.7-1.9%, long-term 0.7% postpaid by 2026.

On subscriber acquisition cost trends, our blended SAC was $428 per gross add, down 14% year-over-year from $498 and 4% sequentially from $445—sixth straight quarter of moderation via efficiencies, marketing optimizations, and postpaid/FWA mix shift.

Wireless (62% adds): postpaid $312, down 12% YoY on BYOD at 42% and 5G Ultra boosting adds 15% QoQ. Prepaid $185 via Walmart kiosks, down 8% distribution. Broadband/Fixed $612, up modestly but 9% below peak, with self-install 65% adoption saving $45 and AI leads up 22%. NovaStream $198, down 21% YoY on bundles.

Regions: North America $415 strongest; Europe €385 ($420) via JV; APAC $465 limited by India wars; LATAM $380 down 18%.

Optimization via ML in MarTech reallocates 25% of $1.2B marketing to CTV/social at 3x ROI; multi-play at 55% shortens payback to 14 months. Q3 $410-420 guide, full-year $1.65-1.70B spend.

Cost of revenue was $4.72 billion, up 8% YoY and 3% QoQ at 52% of revenue—within guidance for 5G and content investments. Trends: 7% three-year CAGR, sequential slowing; Q3 '22 $4.37B (51%), Q4 $4.51B (52%), Q1 '23 $4.58B (52%), Q2 $4.59B (51%), Q3 $4.72B (52%).

Splits: Network ops $2.12B (+10% YoY) from 5G SA D&A $1.1B (+12%), energy $450M (+15%), offset by NFV 8% savings; NA stable, APAC +18% spectrum. Content $1.42B (+7%) NBA/UFC $650M (+11%), OTT $520M (+9%); Europe FX offset by synergies. CPE/Interconnect $710M (+4%), subsidies $150/handset, peering savings $15M.

Initiatives: Cloud-native 35% core for 15-20% D&A efficiency; edge co-lo saves $40M; solar 7% energy cut. Q4 $4.75-4.85B, full-year $18.9B; margins trough 48% expanding 200bps '24.

ARPU trends reflect disciplined pricing and bundling. Blended up 4.2% YoY to $58.70, postpaid wireless $58.42 on 5G Ultra; media $14.50-$18 via ad/dynamic insertion and sports. Nexus One bundle drives uplift, family plans 42% adds enhance loyalty.

Finally, dividend sustainability: $2.04/share annual, 4.6% yield up 4%, 12th increase at 6.2% 5-year CAGR vs. peers. $1.8B TTM payout at 52% FCF, coverage 1.9x to 2.2x '24. YTD FCF $4.2B (+12%) from wireless 5.1%, broadband 450K adds. Capex $7.8B YTD (18%) moderating. Regions: U.S. 0.71% churn; Europe €1.2B FCF; LATAM $450M. Leverage 2.6x targeting 2.3x. $2.4B buybacks YTD, TSR 7.2%; guide 5% hike to $2.14, ROIC 11.2% up 150bps.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds—now 85% mid-band, 450 Mbps median per Ookla. Reliability remains high at sub-1% outage in key markets, and we're investing in advanced technologies like Open RAN, NFV/SDN, and edge computing for IoT, XR, and low-latency gaming/media. Massive MIMO and C-band utilization mirror peer strategies, with solar retrofits and AI maintenance cutting energy and ops costs.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. Strong subscriber growth of 1.2 million net adds driven by launches, bundles like Nexus One, and campaigns yielding BYOD 42%, self-install 65%. SAC efficiencies support this. Satisfaction tops industry via personalized perks, rewards program with 5 million members. Partnerships with Disney+, AWS, Singtel, Vodafone expand bundles, multi-play at 55% households. Churn compression to 1.8% blended underscores experience improvements across touchpoints.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your subscriber acquisition costs and your strategy for reducing churn, specifically with regards to the impact on postpaid wireless mixes?

David Kim: Thanks, Emily. On SAC, as Mike detailed, blended at $428 down 14% YoY, postpaid wireless $312 via BYOD at 42% and 5G self-selection—digital CTV/social at 3x ROI. For churn reduction, postpaid at 0.85% leverages network superiority (450 Mbps), Nexus One bundling (0.6% churn), and AI prediction recovering 28%. Multi-play loyalty and sports content keep it sub-0.9%, ahead of peers. This mix shift boosts lifetime value payback to 14 months.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for leveraging AI and automation to improve network efficiency and reduce operational costs, and how does that impact cost of revenue trends?

Lisa Patel: Great question, Raj. AI and automation are core: predictive maintenance cuts outages 45%, NFV/SDN orchestration 8% opex QoQ ($25M avoided), churn models 92% accurate for retention. ML lead scoring lifts conversions 22%, reallocates marketing. On cost of revenue, these shave network ops—35% cloud-native targeting 15-20% D&A efficiency, edge partnerships save $40M transport. Q3 growth slows further, margins expanding as 5G ramps.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sophia Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sophia Lee: Can you discuss the regulatory environment and any potential impacts on your business, including spectrum auctions and EU DMA effects?

John Ramirez: Thanks, Sophia. Regulatory landscape is navigable: U.S. C-band refarming post-$2.1B wins efficiencies capex down to $9.2B '25; BEAD funds 2.5M rural fiber. EU DMA offset by AVOD in Vodafone JV, price caps in Germany via Open RAN stabilizing churn. India auctions at $0.45/MHz competitive. No material hits; diversified mitigates, focus on converged ecosystem outpaces.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. John, would you like to provide closing remarks?

John Ramirez: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities—new launches, churn/SAC discipline, cost control, ARPU growth, and shareholder returns. We are confident in our ability to deliver sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders, with $5.8B run-rate adds and FCF firepower. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
